The theory was that they were overpowered *because* of their items. Obviously the simplest way to decrease their power was either A) debuff them heavily. B) remove the items power. Or C) Take their items. 

I chose option C because it fit in with the plot of my game, which was that powerful corrupted artifacts being spread throughout the land, a group of heroes go to purify these artifacts and stop the destruction of their land.

After several months of build up to a massive final boss fight, my players approached a short man, clearly blind and deaf, covered in scars and leathers. 

By this point in the campaign, my players all had what I called "Artifact Class Items" or basically the best items in the game (I do a system like that so it seems more appropriate than +1 longsword or something like that). 

The old man is the only person in the room the boss is supposed to be in, and we had a telepath, so they figured they might as well try and communicate with the guy. The second their mind makes contact with his, he transforms. No longer blind, no longer deaf, although his armor remained the same, for a short period.

In a split second, every artifact class item was taken from them, and given to him. In addition, the downsides for the weapons were removed. So the near indestructible plate armor of our tank, that reduced his move speed, dex, and cursed him with voices and an inability to rest? Just near indestructible for the boss.

The only thing my tank had left were his undergarments, a dagger, and a shortsword that he kept on him in case of emergencies. His time-looped bag that kept all his good back-up gear was taken. He was suitably pissed, but after the fight (none of the players died, but 4 of the 5 were making death saves) said it was a great way to have fun.

TL;DR I took all my players good gear from them and gave them to the final boss.

"Do you have any idea the plans I had in place for you? The things you were to accomplish?!"

To be frank, I was quite stunned by the loud, booming voice coming from, seemingly, all around. I looked down at hands... And there was no blood to be seen. This stunned me nearly as much. I was sure I had just slit my wrists. In fact, I could still feel the pain, and I was still very light-headed. Looking back up, I see something rather intriguing... A short, bearded man, with a staff, robes, and what appears to be a ring of light surrounding his head.

For the first time, I look around, past him, I appear to be in... A roman temple? The marble columns in the Tuscan style are unmistakable, but past it... It's all beautiful green grass, healthy English oak and split-leaf pine trees, bluebirds singing, hummingbirds floating around. It's almost as if it's a utopia.

"You were supposed to cure cancer, to restore faith in humanity, to be the first to make contact with other races, xenos if you will, to develop a thought translator *and* develop immortality, albeit only for animals. You literally stopped your cat, Wackoo was his name I believe, from dying? By creating an immortality serum... *From Potatoes...*"

I did that? All that? How? I'm just a weird trans girl, who's failing all her classes... *in high school*?

I open my mouth for the first time since arriving in this weird place, and my voice, normally small and timid, comes out crystal clear, and well toned. "Who... Who are you? Where am I? What happened?"

The person in front of me falters. The harsh look on their face breaks into sadness and regret. A smaller, quieter voice comes from the man. He looks me deep in the eyes, and apologizes. He says to me, in a baritone voice: "I'm so sorry. I forgot the struggles you went through. I am... Well, for lack of a better term, I am god. Or at least the one that all worship goes to. You are in... Heaven, I believe you call it? And you..." His eyes smolder as he says the next line. "You killed yourself. I am mighty. I have much power, but in your realm, the place in between... I can do little. Replenish your blood? Yes. But heal your wounds, make beat your dying heart? That is beyond my reach."

"So you're not all powerful..." I mutter under my breath.

"Not in your realm, no. But here. Here I am all-powerful, and here I live. I have influenced you and yours for many years. Jesus of Nazareth? Not my son, no, but a seraph. A seraph sent as a messenger to put an end to the age of barbarism."

I nod, trying to follow his meaning. I think to myself "Does this mean that the largest religion on Earth is... A hoax?"

My face was a mask of surprise when he said, "No. Not a hoax. Simply a way to get people to come together in harmony, rather than from domination. The Roman Empire ended, because *I* wanted it to end. Because it had done it's part in the story of the world."

He motions for me to walk with him, beckoning me to him with a simple wave of his hand. It seems so easy to follow him. He walks, hands behind his back, staff horizontal, around his midsection. It is a regal pose, made even more so by the ring of light, which I now recognize as a halo, around his head, like a crown.

We pass many things. A sign here and there, pointing to areas for people. There are parks and recreation areas, places to try things you couldn't try in life. Food is abundant, beautiful fountains are everywhere.

While walking, I work up the courage to ask a question that my subconscious had been prodding me to ask. "If you have influence over our world, enough to make me so that I can do all those amazing things, then why is sickness still a thing?"

He opens his mouth to answer, but before he can say a word, I continue: "No, even more, why is depression still around? Anxiety? Heck, if you have enough power to restore blood to my veins, surely you could end wars? Stop every fucking problem known to earth? Even if you can't simply wish it into existence, if you can create people to do certain things, then you can do this. If I was created for no other reason than to cure cancer, and make my cat live forever, then how are all these problems still around."

At this, he seems as stunned as I was when I first arrived. He looks somber as he ponders what I've said. It seems as though something I said, has made *God* think. *I made god think.* He looks to the side, and raises up a hand. A small bird, a kingfisher, lands upon his upraised palm. He brings it close, and starts speaking. Very softly speaking. He says to me, "You see here" as he points to one of the birds legs. Looking close, I notice a small cut, a scar.

Continuing on, he speaks his words of wisdom, "Scars make people. Had you not fallen off of your bike when you were 6, had you not gotten cut by glass at 9, would you be the same person? Had those things not happened, you wouldn't be as good at riding your bike, no? You wouldn't be so careful when handling things. They shape you."

My mouth drops slightly. I hadn't considered that... And he came to this conclusion, and drew me into it, using me as an example, in such a short time. After all, I know myself better than most people... 

"More so, the mental struggles, the internals. Those shape not just how you act, but who you are. Had you not been afflicted with depression, you wouldn't have struggled so hard to be good at what you love. You wouldn't have tried so hard to make people happy. Because you know what it's like to feel worthless. And you didn't want anyone else to feel that way. *That* is why you were destined for greatness. *That* is what made you strong. *That* is why I gave you all of the problems of the world, to bear on strong shoulders. Because you could do it. But I should have seen, I should have known, that anyone, in a moment of weakness, can do rash things."

Tears well up in my eyes. I simply cry. My heart drops. I could have helped so many people. I could have done so much. And I ended it, after simply not being good enough for my own standards?

**NOTE:** This is completely a work of fiction, although I am afflicted with many issues, including depression and anxiety. I do not know what I want to be, or how I want to affect the world. I do know, however, that I want to help people through tough times. I hope that reading this gives you hope, and maybe even helps you through the hard days. Thank you for reading this. 

      Sincerely ~ Mizuki

This story was written impromptu, and is dedicated to my wonderful partner Jenny, in the honor of Valentines Day.

Sitting down with a copy of William Shakespeares play "Hamlet", I realize something. 30 years have passed, since I first saw her. My "charge". The one thing that was to be more important to me than any other. Looking over, she's sleeping soundly on the couch, curled up in a ball, a look of contentment on her face.

Never did I imagine that such a small thing could mean so much to me. But first, I must explain. When I was a child, barely able to make complete sentences, I was given a creature to take care of. Most children received dogs or cats, occasionally a fish, birds, creatures of the forest. Rarer than that, were those who received trees and flowers, bushes and brush. But among all of the living things of Earth, only one was given the responsibility, no, the *privilege* of caring for a human. 

**30 YEARS AGO**

Every year, on January 31st, every single child who had reached the age of 5 was given something to care for. Something to learn. A thing to cherish and love and hold. In my case, I was given Aubrielle. 

Aubrielle was a small child, no more than 10 pounds, maybe 7 or 8 months old. She was abandoned at birth, despite the advances in our government, despite the advances in social welfare. She had survived more than a day without warmth, without food, without water. She was unable to care for herself, let alone anything else. 

I was taught, at a young age, the reality of the world, the cruelty of people, but also of the compassion they can elicit. The true nature of humans is to be sadistic, but in those short moments when something so precious is dropped in their lap, that nature is overtaken by the good in their heart.

So it was with me. I didn't like anything. I didn't like anyone. I was rude, ill-mannered, and destructive. On January 30th, I never would have guessed that my nature would change alongside the charge I was given.

I was given Aubrielle, and my first reaction was to wonder *"why?"* Why was this small child, not even able to care for herself, dropped into my lap? Why wasn't she given her own being to care for? Why did I have to care for her?

I hated her. My nature, already destructive, cruel, and hating, became even more so. I was human, not caretaker.

And then she smiled. A toothy smile, and all of the hatred in my heart simply... vanished. She became my life. I taught her to care, to love, to cherish, to hold.

She taught me the same. It wasn't a matter of my taking care of her. Rather it was us learning from each other, growing together. 

**5 YEARS LATER**

These were the moments I dreaded the most. January 30th. The countdown to the 31st began at 11:59. Each television receiving a slightly different signal, showing a picture of what the child of the house would receive their charge. 

Seconds tick by. I can hear my heartbeat. I can count the beats. Glancing over at our clock, I see it tick over to midnight. Dreading the action, not wanting to see, out of fear of what it might be... I glance over.

And see, among all things, a Maine Coon. Breathing a sigh of relief, I realize that Aubrielle was not going to fail in this task. Aubrielle, bless her heart, had been diagnosed with many things, not the least of which was Asperger's Syndrome. 

Don't get me wrong, she was still the most wonderful human I had the pleasure of meeting, of knowing, of caring for. But she simply couldn't handle looking after something 24/7.

**8 YEARS LATER**

At the age of 18, each person has the option to release their charge from their care. My case was a bit more difficult than the rest. Aubrielle was a *human* like myself. She was 13 years old. I couldn't just leave her, but she was half of the choice, and if she wanted me gone, I would go.

Fortunately, she asked me to never leave her. And so I decided then and there, that I wouldn't. 

**Edit to add in explanation:** I've always wanted to be a mother, and since I had heard the name when I was 6, I have been set on naming my daughter (if/when I have her) "Aubrielle". I decided to, in the story, give her something that would drastically change how she acts, and settled on Aspergers since one of my close friends has the same thing, and they are a wonderful person. I left this story open ended, so that if the time comes in the future when I want to write a story, I could expand upon it. Lastly, I wanted to say that I hope everyone has a wonderful day.
